newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ parliament to debate deferring tax cuts.
newsitem.headline: NZ parliament to debate deferring tax cuts.

text.p: New Zealand's parliament on Wednesday will begin debating the bill to postpone $1.1 billion in tax cuts for a year, parliamentary sources said.
The bill, known as the Taxation (Income Tax Rates) Bill, will be debated under urgency, meaning the debate will continue with extended sessions of parliament until it is concluded.

It proposes deferring the July 1, 1997 tax cuts until July 1, 1998. The postponement is covered under an agreement struck during the coalition talks between the conservative National Party and nationalist New Zealand First.
The coalition agreed to defer the cuts to allow extra spending in this year's budget withour fuelling inflation.
Treasurer Winston Peters on Tuesday released the budget policy statement unveiling plans to spend an extra $950 million in the 1997/98 year.
If a referendum on compulsory superannuation to be held in September delivers a yes vote, the cuts will coincide with the introduction of compulsory superannuation contributions.
